data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word 'malakos' meaning soft or tender. In Greek mythology, Malissia was a young goddess who embodied gentleness and nurturing qualities. The name Malissia carries the meaning “Young goddess” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Malissia usually hope their child will grow to embody young goddess and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Malissia belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Young goddess.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Malissia total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.
